title: Diagnostic relevance and limitations of myosonography in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy
summary:
Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (myositis) are a group of diseases whose common symptom and usually first manifestation is chronic inflammation of the skeletal muscles, which leads to progressive weakness, particularly of the muscles close to the trunk. The disease is divided into the major subgroups of dermatomyositis, polymyositis and inclusion body myositis. There is also overlap syndrome, necrotizing myositis and antisynthetase syndrome.  
Muscle ultrasound is a standardized examination in the diagnosis of myositis, which is performed as part of routine diagnostics. The aim is to assess the degree of connective tissue remodeling of the skeletal muscles in patients with muscle diseases. Muscle ultrasound is also used in everyday clinical practice to select biopsy sites for muscle biopsies and to show signs of inflammation, such as hypervascularization. The Heckmatt scale is used to classify muscle changes into four degrees of severity. 
Myosonography is performed in a standardized manner at our center on the upper and lower extremities on defined muscles and assesses possible connective tissue remodelling of the muscles based on echogenicity. 
The aim of this research project is to investigate the severity of changes in muscle ultrasound in patients with myositis who are treated at our neuromuscular center. The aim is to clarify whether muscle ultrasound is suitable as a prognostic parameter in patients with myositis and what limitations exist in the diagnostic significance of the method with regard to the classification of the individual disease subgroups and statements about clinical progression. 
The question will be addressed by collecting retrospective patient data.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Completed muscle ultrasound
Diagnosed myositis
Exclusion criteria:
Unclear neuromuscular disorder
No muscle ultrasound performed
